quick_notes.title: Circulatory System
quick_notes.detail: Heart, Blood, and Blood Vessels. Human heart has 4 chambers (2 Atria, 2 Ventricles). Arteries : Carry oxygenated blood AWAY from heart (Except Pulmonary Artery). Veins : Carry deoxygenated blood TOWARDS heart (Except Pulmonary Vein).
quick_notes.explanation: The circulatory system is your body's transportation network, made up of the heart, blood, and blood vessels like arteries and veins. The human heart has four chambers: the two upper chambers are called atria (each one is an atrium), which receive blood, and the two lower chambers are called ventricles, which pump blood out. Arteries are blood vessels that carry blood away from the heart; normally this blood is rich in oxygen, except for the pulmonary artery, which carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs. Veins are blood vessels that carry blood toward the heart; normally this blood is low in oxygen, except for the pulmonary vein, which carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart.

quick_notes.title: Blood Components
quick_notes.detail: Plasma (Liquid). RBCs (Erythrocytes - carry O2 via Hemoglobin). WBCs (Leucocytes - immunity). Platelets (Thrombocytes - clotting). RBC life span ~120 days.
quick_notes.explanation: Blood is made of a liquid part called plasma and three types of cells. Red Blood Cells (RBCs), also called erythrocytes, carry oxygen from your lungs to the rest of your body using a special protein called hemoglobin. White Blood Cells (WBCs), also

quick_notes.title: Blood Groups (Landsteiner)
quick_notes.detail: A, B, AB, O. AB+ is Universal Recipient. O- is Universal Donor. Rh factor (Rhesus monkey).
quick_notes.explanation: Blood groups are categories of blood based on the presence or absence of specific markers called antigens on the surface of red blood cells. The main blood group system, discovered by Karl Landsteiner, has four types: A, B, AB, and O. A person with type A blood has the A antigen, type B has the B antigen, type AB has both A and B antigens, and type O has neither antigen. The Rh factor, named after the Rhesus monkey used in early research, is another antigen that can be present (positive, +) or absent (negative, -). A person with AB positive blood has both A and B antigens and the Rh factor, so they can receive blood from any donor, making them the universal recipient. A person with O negative blood has no A, B, or Rh antigens, so their blood can be given to any patient, making them the universal donor.

quick_notes.title: Excretory System
quick_notes.detail: Kidneys (filtering unit), Ureters, Bladder, Urethra. Basic unit of Kidney : NEPHRON.
quick_notes.explanation: The excretory system removes waste from your body. The kidneys are the main filtering organs, and each kidney contains about one million tiny filtering units called nephrons that clean your blood to make urine. From each kidney, a thin tube called a ureter carries the urine down to the bladder, which is a stretchy bag that stores the urine until you are ready to release it. Finally, when you urinate, the urine travels out of your body through a tube called the urethra.

quick_notes.title: Waste Products
quick_notes.detail: Urea is produced in the Liver and filtered by the Kidney. Dialysis is the artificial filtration used when kidneys fail.
quick_notes.explanation: Urea is a waste product made in the liver when the body breaks down proteins. The kidneys then filter this urea out of the blood and remove it from the body in urine. If a person's kidneys stop working properly, they cannot filter waste like urea on their own. In that case, a medical treatment called dialysis is used to artificially clean the blood by removing waste products and extra fluid. Dialysis acts as an external kidney to keep the blood safe until a transplant or recovery happens.
